supply_chain_design.label: Practice 7
supply_chain_design.text: Students engaged with a wide range of topics across optimization modeling, cost analysis, and procurement strategy, with most conversations focused on carrier cost comparisons, constraint formulation, breakeven analysis, and Goal Seek applications. The most common area of difficulty was understanding how to translate business requirements into mathematical constraints—particularly around capacity bounds, truckload minimums, and the relationship between index variables and cost functions—though most students resolved this through Socratic guidance. A secondary pattern emerged around Excel Goal Seek: several students asked the same question repeatedly across multiple turns, suggesting confusion about how to set up the tool or interpret its output, and they benefited from reframing rather than repetition of the same explanation. A few students also struggled with distinguishing between formula structure and numerical values, and with generalizing hard-coded numbers into parameterized formulations. Overall, the assignment drew substantive engagement on modeling and financial reasoning, with most confusion rooted in translating problem logic into constraint syntax rather than computational skill.

supply_chain_design.text: Students engaged with a broad range of cost accounting topics across this practice set, with most conversations centering on activity-based costing (ABC), cost driver identification and calculation, and the cash conversion cycle metrics (DIO, DSO, DPO). Many students worked through traditional versus ABC costing comparisons, cost pool allocation, and balance sheet impacts of transactions. The most consistent area of difficulty was distinguishing between cost drivers and understanding how to apply them correctly in ABC frameworks; several students also struggled with the orders-versus-order-lines distinction and with translating cost-to-serve calculations into actionable insights. A smaller number of conversations were derailed by platform or technical issues unrelated to the content itself. Overall, tutoring quality was strong when substantive engagement occurred, with most tutors using Socratic questioning effectively, though a few conversations included instances where tutors confirmed exact numerical answers or enumerated reasoning steps rather than prompting students to derive them independently.
